[edit | edit source]
Bordeaux Montaigne University was established in 1970 after a restructuring of public universities in and near the city of Bordeaux. The university was known as Université de Bordeaux 3 during its first two decades. In 1990, it took on the name of philosopher Michel de Montaigne who was a native of the modern-day Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, becoming Université Michel de Montaigne Bordeaux 3. In 2014, the university's name was simplified to Université Bordeaux Montaigne after the universities of Bordeaux 1, 2, and 4 were all merged to become the University of Bordeaux. Bordeaux Montaigne University celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2020.[4]

value.text:
Bordeaux Montaigne University (Université Bordeaux Montaigne) is a public university in Pessac, France, southwest of central Bordeaux. Its teaching and research concentrate on the arts, literature, languages and humanities, alongside geography, spatial and urban planning, communication and journalism. Most teaching and research takes place on the Pessac campus. The journalism and technology institutes are based in central Bordeaux, while smaller teaching sites are also identified in Agen and Bayonne.

The institution emerged from the restructuring of the former University of Bordeaux in the early 1970s. Initially known as Université de Bordeaux 3, it adopted the name of Michel de Montaigne in 1990. Its name became Université Bordeaux Montaigne on 12 March 2014, following the merger of three other Bordeaux universities into the University of Bordeaux. Bordeaux Montaigne remained a distinct institution.

The university offers bachelor's, vocational bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees, as well as additional certificates. Its organization has included three teaching and research units since the 2010 academic intake: Humanités, Langues et Civilisations, and Sciences des territoires et de la communication. Doctoral education is organized through the Montaigne–Humanités doctoral school, formed by merging two earlier doctoral schools.
